patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports difficulty in combing hair and reaching objects on high shelves for the past few months. Admits to a sedentary lifestyle.

Secondary_Symptoms: Decreased range of motion in shoulder

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Diabetes mellitus type II, obesity, hypertension. On metformin, insulin, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Sedentary lifestyle, predominately staying indoors and watching television.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies recent injuries or trauma to the arm or shoulder. No fever, weight loss, or other joint involvement.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with stiffness in his arm impacting daily activities.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: Doctor: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on? Patient: I’ve been having stiffness in my arm for a few months, and it’s gotten harder to comb my hair and reach things on higher shelves. I also feel like my shoulder range of motion is decreased, and my arm strength is about 4 out of 5.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often find yourself needing to rush to the bathroom to urinate, even when your bladder doesn't feel completely full?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I haven’t been rushing to urinate or feeling an urgent need when my bladder isn’t very full. My main issue has been the stiffness and reduced shoulder motion that makes daily tasks like combing my hair and reaching overhead harder.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any firm or hard areas in your breast tissue, perhaps a lump that doesn't feel like it's going away?
turns.patient_answer: Doctor: Have you noticed any firm or hard areas in your breast tissue, perhaps a lump that doesn't feel like it's going away? Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any lumps or hard areas in my breast tissue. My concern has mainly been the arm stiffness and limited shoulder motion affecting things like combing my hair and reaching overhead.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any small, firm bumps on your skin that are smooth to the touch?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any small, firm bumps on my skin—nothing smooth to the touch like that. My symptoms have mostly been stiffness and trouble moving my shoulder enough to comb my hair and reach higher shelves.

turns.doctor_question: I've got to make sure I understand what's going on with your body. Can you tell me if you've been having trouble cooling down lately, like if you feel hot and can't seem to get comfortable no matter what you do?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t been feeling hot or unable to cool down—I feel comfortable most of the time. My main problem is the stiffness in my arm and the reduced shoulder movement that makes combing my hair and reaching overhead difficult.”

turns.doctor_question: How have you been feeling lately, emotionally speaking? Have you been experiencing a lot of pressure or anxiety in your daily life?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling unusually anxious or under a lot of pressure lately. It’s mostly the arm stiffness and trouble reaching overhead that bothers me most, and it’s made me more inactive.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching sensations on your skin lately, either all over or in specific areas?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any itching sensations on my skin—either all over or in specific spots. My symptoms have stayed focused on the arm and shoulder stiffness that makes combing my hair and reaching high shelves difficult.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any unusual spots, rashes, or lesions on your arms, particularly along the veins?
turns.patient_answer: I haven’t noticed any unusual spots, rashes, or lesions on my arms, including along the veins. My main issue is still the stiffness and decreased shoulder range of motion that makes combing my hair and reaching high shelves difficult.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that it's been harder for you to find the right words when you're talking lately? Sometimes people have trouble getting the word out that they want to say. Is that something you've been experiencing?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had trouble finding the right words when I’m talking. My issues have stayed mainly with the stiffness in my arm and my shoulder range of motion, which makes combing my hair and reaching overhead harder.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your muscles feel stiff or tense, even when you're trying to relax or move around?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: Yes, my arm feels stiff even when I try to relax, and it’s hard to get my shoulder moving normally. It tends to make everyday tasks like combing my hair and reaching overhead much more difficult.

turns.doctor_question: How's your energy level been today? Have you felt unusually sleepy or struggled to stay awake?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: My energy has been pretty normal—I’m not unusually sleepy. The stiffness and reduced shoulder movement are what limit me most, and they make me want to stay inactive.

turns.doctor_question: Can you tell me if one or both of your legs feel warmer than usual right now?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed my legs feeling warmer than usual—my discomfort is mainly in my arm, with stiffness and decreased shoulder range of motion that makes combing my hair and reaching overhead difficult.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you find that you're coughing up mucus or phlegm, or is your cough mostly dry?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any cough or mucus/phlegm—my symptoms are focused on my arm and shoulder stiffness that’s been making it hard to comb my hair and reach overhead.”
